en.html:
...I sat among trees. Hikaru lay in my arms, breathing in sleep.

Sat—perhaps not the right word. Perhaps I had simply become unable to move.

My leg muscles were completely taut. Even standing looked unlikely. How far had I run? Scratches covered me; I had bled considerably.

Consciousness had gone missing. From leaving the Horigoe residence with Hikaru until this instant, staring blankly around—an absolute blank. Nothing remained.

Surely I could not have run for more than a whole day. It must still be the same night. Probably several hours... No, perhaps much less.

Hardly more than a guess, but the surroundings felt like Izu, not very different from Horigoe.

……俺は木々の中、座り込んでいた。
　腕の中には光がいて、寝息を立てている。

　座っていた――というのは、違うかもしれない。
　単に動けなくなっただけとも思えた。

　足の筋肉は完全に張り、立ち上がる事さえままなり
そうにない。
　どれほどの距離を駆け巡ったのか。あちらこちら傷
だらけで、出血も酷かった。

　意識は飛んでいる。
　光を抱えて堀越御所を飛び出してから――いま呆然
と周囲を見回しているこの瞬間まで。記憶は全き空白
で、何も残っていなかった。

　まさか丸一日以上走り続けていたとは考えられない
から、まだ同じ夜の内であろう。
　おそらく、あれから数時間程……いや、実はもっと
短いのかもしれない。

　ほとんど勘でしかないが、辺りの風土も伊豆のもの、
堀越のそれとそう違いはないと思える。

en.html:
—What should I do now?

A foolish question in every sense. No need to ask now. Not something to ask now. Asking now accomplished nothing.

The answer was plain.
What I had to do was perfectly clear.

Therefore I stopped thinking.
No need for that answer—I did not want it.

Did not want to know.
Even if I knew already... while pretending ignorance remained possible, let me have that much.

I adjusted Hikaru in my arms and lowered my face. Quiet sleeping breath touched my cheek.

A little sleep.
The necessary thinking could wait until afterwards.

Now, sleep. Rest in one final illusion.
Like this... forever. Forever protecting Hikaru...

Smiling, Hikaru said it. Arms spread, as though savoring the mountain's night wind.

Hikaru.

...<ruby>Silver Star<rt>Hikaru</rt></ruby>.

The Silver Star said to be Hikaru Minato's dream. Standing in the moonlight, she certainly looked dreamlike.

But nothing there was empty or weak.
Power. Power enough to overflow!

This was a dream's existence?
Something so full of strength?

Was I not the one who had dreamed something strange? Wandering into these mountains, <ruby>deceived<rt>bewitched</rt></ruby> by foxes and badgers...

That explanation—was much easier to accept just now.

Kageaki"Your father..."
Hikaru"Yes."
Hikaru"Recover the father taken from me."
Kageaki"..."
Kageaki"Your father... was not taken..."
Hikaru"..."
Kageaki"Lord Akitaka will not reject you! Go to him, and he will receive you at any time..."
Hikaru"Meeting him is not my wish."
Hikaru"For him to name himself my father. Recognize Hikaru as his daughter."
Kageaki"That also—"
Hikaru"Can come true?"
Kageaki"............"
Hikaru"As you say, I can meet him whenever I please. Meet him, call him Father. Yet I have never done it."
Hikaru"Rejection frightens me."
Kageaki"..."
Hikaru"What do you think, Kageaki?"
Hikaru"Will Hikaru's wish come true? Will Father, from his heart, in truthful words—acknowledge me as his daughter...?"
